summary: The Gemara establishes that the incense must be placed on the coals inside the Holy of Holies (refuting the Sadducee position), the cloud of incense must fill the space before the High Priest approaches the ark, and the 'no man in the Tent of Meeting' exclusion applies only during the incense burning - not during blood sprinkling.

display.whats: Must the incense be lit inside the Holy of Holies, and how complete must the cloud be before the High Priest approaches the ark?
display.hint: The Sages derive from 'before God' that the incense must be placed inside - the Sadducees wanted to prepare it outside first. The cloud requirement is absolute: if it does not fill the space, the rite is incomplete. The 'no man' prohibition applies only during burning.
display.title: Inside the Cloud: Where Incense Atones

learning.ahaMoment: The incense rite embodies a theological principle: even the High Priest cannot approach the divine presence without mediation. The smoke cloud is not protection from danger - it is the act of reverence itself.
learning.memoryAnchor: The cloud of incense must fill the entire space of the Holy of Holies before the High Priest approaches the ark - the rite cannot be rushed.
learning.learnerQuestion: Must the incense be lit inside the Holy of Holies, and how complete must the cloud be before the High Priest approaches the ark?
learning.coreTension: The Sadducees held the incense should be lit outside so the High Priest enters already wrapped in smoke, while the verse 'before God' must be reconciled with the 'no man' exclusion and with how complete the cloud must be before any approach to the ark.
learning.coreMove: The Gemara reads 'before God' as requiring the incense to be placed on the coals inside the Kodesh Kodashim itself, reads 'so the cloud covers' as requiring the fill to be complete before approach, and limits the 'no man' exclusion to the duration of the burning itself.

takeaway.text: The incense must be placed on the coals inside the Holy of Holies, not prepared outside; the cloud must fill the space completely before the High Priest approaches the ark; the 'no man' exclusion applies only during the burning, not throughout the whole service.

learning.learningBlocker: Learners may assume the 'no man' prohibition excludes everyone from the Tent of Meeting for the entire Yom Kippur Holy of Holies service, missing that it applies specifically during the incense burning.

misconceptions.misconception: The 'no man' prohibition excludes anyone from the Tent of Meeting throughout the whole Yom Kippur service, including during the blood sprinkling.
misconceptions.correction: The 'no man' verse applies only during the incense burning itself - it does not apply during the blood sprinkling that follows.

glossary.en: The gold cover of the Ark of the Covenant, with two cherubim on top; the cloud of incense covered this on Yom Kippur.
The incense offering burned on Yom Kippur inside the Holy of Holies; placed on coals, its cloud covered the ark.
Evil speech, slander; according to the Gemara, incense atones for this sin specifically.

rashiTranslations.en: 'One might think even in the entire courtyard' - a person should not stand while the priest burns the incense
in the innermost sanctuary. 'I have only that it applies during the burning of the incense' - further on it explains
what this implies: 'you must say this refers to the burning of the incense,' since the giving of the blood is not
uniform across all of them, since the bull atones for him and for the priests and the goat for Israel.
'Concerning slander' - like that of Korach,
it was slander, as it is written (Numbers 17),
'you have killed the people of the Lord'; and unspecified slander
is spoken in secret. 'From between the Entrance Hall
and the Altar' - the entire air-space of twenty-two cubits
between them. 'This was only taught regarding the burning
of the Sanctuary' - the inner altar's morning and evening incense,
since it is close to it. 'But during the burning
of the innermost sanctuary' - from the Sanctuary, since it is close
to it, they separate; but from between the Entrance Hall and the Altar,
which is farther away, they do not separate. 'At the time of giving the blood of the bull
of the anointed priest' - the one brought for erring in one of the commandments
in his own ruling and acting on it, whose blood is given
on the curtain and on the golden altar. 'And the goats of
idol worship' - a community that worshipped idols
on a ruling of the court brings a bull as a burnt offering
and a goat as a sin offering, as it is written in the portion Shelach
Lecha Anashim (ibid. 15); and that goat's
blood is given on the curtain and it is not eaten, as we derive
in the Sifra and Sifrei and in tractate Zevachim
(47a). 'So what distinction is there,' etc. -
this 'ha' is like 'harei,' meaning, now
what distinction is there in the separation between the Sanctuary
and the Entrance Hall and the Altar. 'Whether during
the burning,' etc. - he assumed it meant either
during the burning of the innermost sanctuary, or
not during the burning of the innermost sanctuary
but during the giving of the blood of the innermost sanctuary.
'And from between the Entrance Hall and the Altar they do not separate' - meaning
regarding the innermost sanctuary, except during its burning,
but not during the giving of the blood. 'Does this not mean,'
etc. - as I explained. 'No, during the burning
of the Sanctuary' - meaning that they separate from between the Entrance Hall
and the Altar, and this is what it teaches: just as they separate
from between the Entrance Hall during the burning of the Sanctuary,
so too they separate during the giving of the blood of the
anointed priest's bull, which is also performed in the Sanctuary. 'If so' -
since just as they separate during the burning it refers to the Sanctuary
and not to the innermost sanctuary, then 'what
distinction is there' - said with astonishment, as if to say is there no further distinction
besides the one that not during the burning
of the innermost sanctuary the teaching states that in the Sanctuary they separate
both during its own burning and during
the innermost sanctuary's burning, and not during its burning,
meaning during the giving of the blood, whether of the Sanctuary
or of the innermost sanctuary; whereas from between the Entrance Hall
and the Altar they do not separate except not during
the burning, which is the time of the giving of the blood
of the innermost sanctuary, but only during the burning
of the Sanctuary, for even during that burning
there is a further distinction, since from the Sanctuary they separate, etc.
'It does indeed teach this' - he says this affirmatively; this is indeed what it means: this 'not during the burning' that it states
means not during the burning of the Sanctuary, but rather it is during the burning of the innermost sanctuary.
'Whether during the burning' - of the Sanctuary; and this 'not during the burning' that the tanna teaches
means not its own burning, but rather during the burning of the innermost sanctuary.
